notes: Tool execution in this review session returned no output for every Bash/Read/Glob call, so this is a static review of the pasted diff; the builder's reported GREEN/ruff results and the content SHA256 could not be independently re-executed here. The fixed verifier should confirm tests/ruff.

Authorization path is sound: authorize() re-resolves the grant via the injected lookup on every call (test asserts 5 lookups across success/stale/revoked/missing), pins grant_id+revision with bool-as-int rejected before comparison, denies expiry equality and revocation at its instant, rejects unknown/malformed permission levels before level_allows, and uses only resolve_principal_permission (no bare-actor or local-admin fallback). replace(current) re-runs PilotGrant.__post_init__, so a mutated lookup result (model_egress_allowed=1) is rejected as tested.

Provenance is enforced: _identifier rejects '://' and wildcards, validate_claims binds every claim to the frozen SourceSet and rejects unknown IDs, SourceSet rejects duplicate source_id and namespace/purpose/window/audience drift, and nested TimeWindow/SourceRef/Principal instances are re-validated via replace()/re-construction.

Non-blocking edge: TimeWindow.__post_init__ only catches ValueError/ZoneInfoNotFoundError. If the tzdata pip package is importable, a directory-name key such as TimeWindow(START, END, 'America') makes zoneinfo._common.load_tzdata open a directory and leak IsADirectoryError instead of SchemaError. Consider catching OSError as well.

Non-blocking edge: on a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS) ZoneInfo('utc') or 'america/los_angeles' resolves and is stored as the non-canonical key, while the same value fails on Linux; the model does not canonicalize display_timezone.

Non-blocking gap: SourceSet does not require its sources to share grant_id/grant_revision, so a set can mix evidence collected under different grants; A01 acceptance did not list grant consistency, but a later task should bind SourceRef.grant_id/revision to the authorized grant.

Non-blocking: _permission_levels accepts 2-part legacy 'actor:level' pairs, which resolve_principal_permission then ignores with a UserWarning on every authorize call; fail-closed behavior is correct (tested) but the warning will be emitted per request in production if legacy grants remain configured.
